column1: # BASELINE of QUOTE-PIN keys -- drafted r7125+70.1 (node 70) on the mutation instrument's --quote operator.  Data, not code.
# ** A RECORD OF ADJUDICATIONS, NOT A LIST OF EXEMPTIONS ** -- the same rule as prose_pin_baseline.tsv.
#   One line per key:  receipt <TAB> literal (JSON) <TAB> target <TAB> tier <TAB> flags <TAB> verdict <TAB> what was read
# ** WHAT A QUOTE-PIN IS. **  An asserting test of a string literal's PRESENCE in text the receipt reads from a file it
# does not own.  target PAPER = corpus/*.tex; SOURCE = any other file (a receipt's code, a ledger, a PREDICTION).
# tier SENTENCE = three or more words (wording another seat owns); TOKEN = a label, name, macro or figure.
# flag ALT = the test is one arm of a disjunction of paper states (the repaired form, which passes in either state);
# flag OPEN = the literal carries an openness marker (conjecture, open, owed, remains, ...).
# flag XOR = an EXCLUSIVE disjunction (`(A and B) != C`) -- the form that went red at r7125 when a third state made both true.
#   UNADJUDICATED  not yet read.  ** The only bucket that means work, and its count may only FALL. **
#   DELIBERATE     the wording IS the claim: a NAME (a receipt key inside \rcpt{}, a label, a macro), a value, or a
#                  quotation of a record shown not to move (the quoted LINE written once and never altered, traced
#                  literal by literal on the FULL history -- not the file's commit count, which says nothing about whether
#                  an append-only row moves, and never a shallow clone's graft root, r7283).  ** NOT a quoted
#                  definition or a falsifier: a meaning-preserving reword of a definition leaves it standing, so such a
#                  pin is a proposition and is MEANING-HELD (r7251 ①, r7271 ruling ②).  And a receipt's declared purpose
#   ALT-OK         a disjunction over legitimate paper states that admits the state the result itself may produce.
#                  ** States of ONE text (r7271 ruling ②).  A disjunction over TWO papers stating one proposition is not
#                  ALT-OK: each arm is verdicted as the proposition pin it is. **
#   REPAIR-OWED    pins a sentence whose meaning, not wording, is the claim.  Owed a rewrite to what it is for.
#                  ** Three shapes the grain clause does not reach take it in this general sense (r7271 ruling ②): a
#                  CO-OCCURRENCE pin, two short spans whose conjunction in a FILE stands for one claim made in one sentence;
#                  a span or ALT arm that cannot FAIL (a common word, the mirror of the dangling arm that cannot fire); and
#                  an OBJECT-dangling span, subject named and object a pronoun.  Each repair is a widening. **
#                  ** And the NARROWER-THAN-CLAIM family, of which cannot-fail is the extreme (r7271-r7285, 69's batches):
#                  ⓐ the PROXY -- a name, term or heading standing for a proposition, able to fail but carrying less than
#                  the claim ("Brown and Kucha", "WHAT IT CANNOT DO"); ⓑ the DISJUNCTION pinning a CONJUNCTION -- the label
#                  claims both, the check is an `or`; ⓒ the DEAD or UNDECIDING ALT arm -- an arm occurring nowhere, or one
#                  that is a substring of its partner, or one `or`-ed with a partner that cannot fail; ⓓ the arm behind a
#                  VACUOUS GUARD, never evaluated (its repair is the guard, routed as a receipt defect); ⓔ (the FIFTH
#                  variant, r7285 ruling ③) a COMPLETE CLAUSE THAT DROPS ITS OWN CONDITION -- subject named, clause whole,
#                  and the qualifier the claim rests on outside the span ("the leaf's transverse-traceless mode evolves by
#                  a wave equation", where the paper conditions it on "a wave that one residual isometry still pins" and
#                  the claim is that the CONFINED case is exhibited).  None of ⓐ-ⓔ is reached by the subject rule. **
#   NOT-A-PIN      (r7131+70.1, 70) the operator's false positive: not a test of another seat's wording at all (a parse guard,
#                  an absence claim written as `== []`, a seed that adapts to the current state).  Counted, not owed.
#   ENCODING-OK    (r7137+70.1, 70) an ALT whose arms are encodings of ONE fact (case, markup, spacing, prefix/full line),
#                  not states of a moving text.  It cannot fail on success.  Counted, not owed.
#   MEANING-HELD   (r7253, 66's ruling ③) a pin whose claim is a MEANING for which NO STRING FORM can carry the finding --
#                  70's registered content-skeleton passes 0 of 3 seeded members, structurally, because a converse keeps every
#                  token.  So REPAIR-OWED on such a row named work nobody can do: the finding is held at its commit, the live
#                  string assertion is a READ TRIGGER rather than a guard, and the key is COUNTED and not owed.
#                  ** THE WHOLE-CLAUSE BOUND (r7283): a row can take MEANING-HELD only if its span passes the subject rule
#                  below, so the MEANING-HELD share of a batch is bounded by how often its receipts pin WHOLE clauses.  A
#                  batch of fragments has MEANING-HELD near zero however many propositions it pins -- they are all there,
#                  and every one lands in REPAIR-OWED first. **
#   ** AND r7253's ruling ② -- THE GRAIN CLAUSE, which decides WHICH of DELIBERATE and REPAIR-OWED a pin takes: DELIBERATE
#      where the pinned span is the SHORTEST that carries its claim AND the claim is an IDENTITY; REPAIR-OWED where a strictly
#      shorter span carries it, the repair being to shorten the span.
#      ⌗ TWO MEASURED LIMITS ON IT, r7253+cc66.171, on P15's 148 contested-cell rows.  ① It is SILENT on (shortest span) AND
#        (claim is a PROPOSITION) -- 44 of the 148 -- where the subject rule governs.  ② Limb two needs a CONTIGUOUS strictly
#        shorter span, because a pin is a SUBSTRING of a document: a redundant span in the MIDDLE of a pinned sentence (an
#        apposition between the subject and the predicate the claim needs) is NOT reachable by the clause and falls into ①. **
#      ⌗ A THIRD LIMIT, 60's, bound in the SAME revision (r7255 ruling ②) and missing from this header until
#        r7255+cc66.175: minimality is measured over WORD-ALIGNED spans, because 70's EXTENDED spans are character
#        windows landing mid-word.  ** SO THE CLAUSE AS BOUND READS: DELIBERATE where the pinned span is the shortest
#        CONTIGUOUS, WORD-ALIGNED span that carries its claim and the claim is an IDENTITY; REPAIR-OWED where a
#        strictly shorter such span carries it. **  A seat reading only limits ① and ② applies an unamended clause.
#   ** THE SUBJECT RULE -- the rule limit ① defers to where the grain clause is silent (written down r7271, 69; rewritten
#      r7285, 69, because a second reader verdicted the same shape the other way: 38 of 60's 153 DELIBERATE/MEANING-HELD
#      rows against 1 of 69's 22, r7285 ruling ②).  APPLY IT AS A TEST, BEFORE ANY SENTENCE-TIER VERDICT, IN THIS ORDER:
#      ⓵ READ THE SPAN'S FIRST WORDS.  If it opens on a predicate or verb ("is ...", "settles ...", "extend ..."), a
#        relative pronoun or subordinator ("which ...", "that ...", "while ...", "As ..."), a participle ("carrying ..."),
#        a preposition, or an appositive or noun phrase whose head sits outside it ("complex-analytic and geometric",
#        "exactly the perturbative regime of ..."), the span is DANGLING.
#      ⓶ FIND THE SUBJECT OF ITS MAIN VERB.  If the subject is outside the span, or is a pronoun, demonstrative or
#        quantifier standing for something named earlier ("it", "this", "they", "these", "all three", "both", "each"),
#        the span is DANGLING; so is a span whose OBJECT is a pronoun ("... frees it").  A verbless absolute phrase whose
#        predicate is outside it ("the ultraviolet definition of the mode sums with them") is dangling on both counts.
#      ⓷ A DANGLING SPAN IS REPAIR-OWED EVEN WHEN IT READS AS A COMPLETE PROPOSITION ON ITS OWN.  This is the case the
#        rule exists for and the one a second reader keeps passing: "settles the in-regime all-orders stability directly"
#        reads complete, and its subject ("it", Friedrich's result) is in the clause before it.  Reading complete is not
#        naming the subject.  Its repair is a widening -- to the clause that names the subject, a pronoun to its
#        antecedent -- after which the row is EXTENDED.  Widening is a SPAN change: the receipt's assertion, tolerance and
#        the document it reads do not move.
#      ⓸ THE VERBLESS APPOSITIVE, ruled here because it is the boundary: an appositive with BOTH of its terms inside the
#        span ("the one non-generic exception, the Nariai branch") is a CLAUSE for this rule -- it names its subject and
#        nothing the claim needs is outside it.  It then takes MEANING-HELD, not DELIBERATE: a reword keeps the
#        identification standing (r7251 ①), and DELIBERATE is for names, values and unmoving records.  An appositive
#        with ONE term inside the span and its head outside is dangling under ⓵.
#      ⓹ ONLY A SPAN THAT PASSES ⓵-⓸ GOES ON TO THE GRAIN CLAUSE and the DELIBERATE / MEANING-HELD question, and even
#        then the narrower-than-claim family under REPAIR-OWED (ⓐ-ⓔ) is checked: a whole clause can still drop its
#        condition.  A quotation of a record shown not to move is DELIBERATE without this test AND without the
#        narrower-than-claim family ⓐ-ⓔ (r7287 ruling ③): its wording, clipped or not, is the record, so a token occurring
#        four times in a frozen record is the record's wording and not a proxy, and a fragment of it is not dangling.
#        The exemption is the LINE's, not the file's: a record-kind file whose quoted line has moved, or a LIVE
#        instrument's docstring whose figure would be corrected (a count that goes stale), gets no exemption. **
#      ⌗ AND AN OPERATIONAL LIMIT, r7255+cc66.172 ①, from performing the 27: limb two needs the shorter span's
#        OCCURRENCE COUNT taken BEFORE the shortening.  On the clause's own cited exemplar the shorter span occurs
#        TWICE where the pinned form occurs once, so shortening converted a pin on the CLAIM into a pin on the FILE.
# ** A RE-STATEMENT APPENDS, IT DOES NOT PREPEND (r7253+cc66.171, after the sixth instance of the fail-on-success class).
#    A re-stated row keeps its ORIGINAL reason and head stamp and carries the new reading after `** RE-STATED ...`, because
#    every per-revision audit receipt in the corpus selects its own rows with `reason.startswith(its stamp)`.  Prepending the
#    new stamp reds another seat's receipt for work THIS seat was ordered to do -- measured: cc66.169's prepend convention
#    would have broken three gates of node 60's `S2` and, through it, one of `S5`. **
# ** THE REPAIR RULE IS NOT NEW: `L-249` (r3105) stated it after nine pin-breaks -- pin the historical state at the commit it
# stood at, assert the CURRENT state separately, and make a directional live check MONOTONE. **
# ** THE KEY IS (receipt, literal), NOT A LINE NUMBER, DELIBERATELY ** -- check_prose_pins' rule, for the same reason.

# ⛭ r7201+70.1 (66's r7197 addition): the receipts' own pin LISTS, keyed by the operator for the first time -- newly COUNTED, not newly written.  Their own bucket, UNADJUDICATED-LIST, so the r7125 backlog other receipts hold monotone (2,167, may only fall) is not raised by a population it never contained.
